summary: Craze & Crash: watched 6 Shorts (Krispy Kreme, Marvel, Blockbuster, Juicero, Spanx, Lipton) next to their drop points; raised the beat-2 lesson with four more cases and queued an ending test.
why: Eight of nine Shorts with drop points lose 19–34% at beat 2 when the picture leaves the hook's subject (Marvel −34.4% at 5.6 s on a 10-K page and 'the decade before'); Krispy Kreme stayed on its truck, lost 12.8%, and holds best (57.4% stayed).

findings.title: Marvel −34.4% at 5.6 s
findings.detail: Captain America cut to a small-type 1997 10-K while the line told the bankruptcy backstory.

findings.title: Blockbuster −20.7% at 6.3 s, stayed 41.9%
findings.detail: Black-and-white founder polaroids and 'So what happened?' replaced the store; 13 points under the 54.8% median.

findings.title: Krispy Kreme is the model
findings.detail: Beat 2 kept the brand on screen (truck + BROKE UP stamp): −12.8%, best stayed 57.4%, held after hook 37.2%.

findings.title: The 3 Shorts made since the lesson comply
findings.detail: Adidas, Crocs and Lipton keep the hook's thing in beat 2; numbers due next run.

findings.title: Ending question costs 6–12%
findings.detail: Every Short loses at the 'X or Y: which…?' ending; queued as a test.

changes.title: Lesson 1 raised
changes.detail: Added Marvel, Blockbuster, Spanx, Juicero; fix now bans backstory lines and black-and-white/archive/document pages as beat 2's main layer.

changes.title: Challenger doc-ending-no-question
changes.detail: End on the payoff and loop, without the ending question.
